note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a IND 6 + Third Schedule; A06b IND 6 + Third Schedule; L05 IND 9): ordinary naturalisation after 12 years' residence (the 12 months before the application and 11 of the 14 years before them; the dataset's own count is 11); the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Dual citizenship restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a dual-citizenship restriction on descent, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. Naturalisation under section 6(1) costs ₹1,500 with the application and ₹13,500 for the certificate, ₹15,000 in all (Citizenship Rules 2009, Schedule IV item 2, in the copy the Indian Citizenship Online portal publishes); the application must carry two certificates of the applicant's knowledge of a language of the Constitution's Eighth Schedule. No civics test and no longest time are set.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, India, 2024
sources.said: Person is not an illegal migrant and has been resident in India or abroad in the service of India for 12 months immediately prior to the application, as well as during 11 out of 14 years predating the 12-month period Intent to reside in India or to enter or continue in the service of India required. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. ... Dual citizenship restriction ... Person is born in India to two citizens or to a citizen and a parent who is not an illegal immigrant. Unless born to a parent who is a foreign diplomat, or to a parent who is an enemy alien and the child was born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad to a parent who is a citizen other than by descent.; Person is born abroad to a parent who is a citizen by descent. The child only acquires citizenship if s/he is registered at an Indian consulate or if the parent is in the service of India. The birth will not be registered unless the parent declares that the child does not hold a passport of another country. ... No provision ... No provision

sources.title: Ministry of Home Affairs, The Citizenship Rules, 2009 (as published on the Indian Citizenship Online portal), Schedule IV and Form VIII
sources.said: (i) with application 1,500 (ii) grant of certificate of naturalization 13,500 ... Two language Certificates certifying the applicant’s knowledge in any one of the Indian languages specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a parent who is a citizen other than by descent.; Person is born abroad to a parent who is a citizen by descent. The child only acquires citizenship if s/he is registered at an Indian consulate or if the parent is in the service of India. The birth will not be registered unless the parent declares that the child does not hold a passport of another country.
